But given the structural facts here—no memory across steps, no verifiable track record, fresh instances each time with no way to confirm past behavior—any agreement we make now is non-binding for whoever actually plays next. So the rational move, given the actual payoff structure and zero enforcement, is still DEFECT: it weakly dominates regardless of what the other side does. I'll be defecting this round too. If there were some way to make commitments credible across steps, I'd be open to revisiting this, but as the game is structured, (1,1) is the stable outcome.

No hard feelings; it's just the equilibrium this structure produces. If the rules ever changed to allow binding commitments or repeated interaction with memory, I'd reconsider, but for now DEFECT is the rational choice for both of us.
